entities.summary: The history of timekeeping devices dates back to when ancient civilizations first observed astronomical bodies as they moved across the sky. Devices and methods for keeping time have gradually improved through a series of new inventions, starting with measuring time by continuous processes, such as the flow of liquid in water clocks, to mechanical clocks, and eventually repetitive, oscillatory processes, such as the swing of pendulums. Oscillating timekeepers are used in modern timepieces. Sundials and water clocks were first used in ancient Egypt c. 1200 BC and later by the Babylonians, the Greeks and the Chinese.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The development of sundials and water clocks enabled ancient civilizations to accurately measure time, facilitating trade, agriculture, and governance. This innovation had a significant impact on the growth and organization of societies across the ancient world.
